hits.title: Buddhism & Science in Dialogue
hits.description: Interdisciplinary approaches to specific social sciences topics in Asian studies. Topics may include comparative analysis of a theme across the countries in Asia or focus on a theme within a single country.

instructorProvidedContent.instructorDescription:
This course examines the complexity and depth of the relationship between Buddhism and science, particularly the extent to which they can be considered compatible. This inquiry will be approached through the perspectives of Buddhist philosophy, Buddhist modernism, and the philosophy of science. The meaning of "Buddhism and science  itself depends on how one defines each term and what it means to put them side-by-side with the conjunction "and.  Nevertheless, for more than a century, scholars and practitioners have brought Buddhism and science together in the varied contexts of quantum mechanics, neuroscience, cognitive science, and psychology. In doing so, they have generally assumed some form of kinship or compatibility, despite the diverse traditions encompassed by Buddhism and the varied domains encompassed by science. Interpretations of this compatibility have spanned a wide spectrum: some argue that the core teachings of Buddhism, despite tensions with certain other doctrines, are not contradicted by modern scientific findings, while others claim that Buddhism can not only be corroborated by scientific discoveries but can also anticipate key future findings and reveal truths inaccessible to scientific methods alone.
Seeking to foster a dynamic dialogue between Buddhism and science, the course will guide students in addressing several key questions: What do we mean by "Buddhism  and "science,  separately and together? How does Buddhism, often described as a science of the inner world, relate to the development of modern science? In the late modern period, Is Buddhism now obliged to be the most "scientific religion ? Is Buddhism's perceived compatibility with science an essential and inevitable aspect of its mystique? And finally, why is it important for us to reflect on the tensions and convergences between Buddhism and science?
To guide students to think through these questions, the course will cover a range of topics including Buddhist epistemology and quantum mechanics, neuroscience and cognitive science in relation to mindfulness, technology and AI in Buddhist studies.
instructorProvidedContent.typicalTopicsAndOrSchedule:
W1 -- Setting the Stage, Challenges for Buddhism and Science, Buddhism and Science in Dialog
W2 -- Buddhist Epistemology and Scientific Inquiry: What Counts as Good Evidence, What is Empirical Inference, Matter, atoms and quantum mechanics I&II 
W3 -- Buddhist Cosmology and Modern Cosmology: Time and space, Mind and Consciousness, Neuroscience of Meditation, Mindfulness
W4 -- Technology and AI, Historical and Cultural Dimensions, Critical Reflections: Limits of Compatibility
